9fe6716f7bff41b986c467afc82c6c357fb19baf.summary: Fortinet's 2014 analysis, republished from Virus Bulletin, describes the Andromeda modular botnet. The loader fetches modules and updates from its C&C server, uses anti-VM and anti-debug checks, injects into trusted processes and sets up autostart. Version 2.06 is the latest official build. Modules include a form grabber, a ring3 rootkit and a SOCKS4 proxy. The bot can also distribute other malware, including ZeroAccess, Kelihos and FakeAV.

9f050b8452d7b63e4d794f66cc4f6c525c51b3a3.summary: A BleepingComputer report (Dec 2021) on ALPHV BlackCat, a Rust-written ransomware-as-a-service operation promoted on Russian-speaking forums. It describes configurable encryption modes, PSExec-based spread across domain networks, disruption of backups and ESXi snapshots, an access token that protects negotiations, and triple extortion including DDoS threats. Victims were reported in the USA, Australia and India. Ransom demands run from $400,000 to $3 million, with affiliates earning 80 to 90 percent. The report judges it very likely to fill the gap left by BlackMatter and REvil.

9fd309f32f02d3c4d87ee342ddce50440291c64f.summary: Cisco Talos describes an attack by the Interlock ransomware group, which first appeared publicly in September 2024. The group used big-game hunting and double extortion. Initial access was a fake Chrome updater RAT, followed by a credential stealer, keylogger, RDP, AnyDesk, PuTTY and Azure AzCopy exfiltration. Talos estimates about 17 days of dwell time, and EDR was disabled on some servers. The ransomware encrypts files, drops ransom notes and demands a response within 96 hours.
